service_upgrade_and_data_preservation_au.label: REAL
evidence: Real, memory-bounded (--memory=512m) ubuntu:24.04 container: install -> real registry+config state created (SHA256 recorded) -> `apt-get install --reinstall` (upgrade simulation) -> SHA256 of both files confirmed byte-identical afterward -> `apt-get remove` (not purge) -> membrane binary confirmed gone, both data files confirmed still present -> reinstall -> registry/config still functional.

registry_schema_versioning.label: REAL
evidence: Real gap found: registry_core.cpp's loader checked schema_version was PRESENT but never checked its VALUE, unlike server_config.cpp's own existing fail-closed check -- a hypothetical future registry format bump would have been silently misparsed rather than rejected.
Fixed: added MEMBRANE_REGISTRY_SCHEMA_VERSION (== 1), registry load now rejects any other value with UNSUPPORTED_SCHEMA, matching server_config.h's own established convention exactly.
New test test_load_unsupported_schema_version_fails_closed in test_registry_core, mirroring test_server_config's pre-existing equivalent test. ASan/UBSan clean.

Migration policy documented in docs/schema-versioning.md: no automatic migration exists or is planned for v0.4 (schema_version has never actually changed since introduction for either file); a future bump's intended path (reject old files clearly, decide migration-vs-manual-regeneration at that time) is documented rather than built speculatively.

reproducible_build_investigation.label: REAL
reproducible_build_investigation.finding: Two back-to-back `cpack -G DEB` runs from an identical, unchanged build tree produced two DIFFERENT .deb files. Root-caused by extracting both: every real file inside (binaries, shared libs, LICENSE.txt) was byte-identical -- the difference was entirely the gzip header's embedded wall-clock build timestamp inside control.tar.gz/data.tar.gz.
reproducible_build_investigation.fix: Setting the standard SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH environment variable before `cpack -G DEB` makes dpkg-deb (>=1.18.19, present on this host) normalize all embedded timestamps, producing a bit-for-bit identical .deb across repeated runs from the same commit -- confirmed via matching SHA256. No CMakeLists.txt change needed. Wired into scripts/build-release.sh (SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH pinned to the release commit's own `git log -1 --format=%ct`).

sbom.label: REAL
evidence: scripts/generate-sbom.py emits a CycloneDX 1.5-shaped JSON populated entirely from real, current repo state: the llama.cpp submodule's actual pinned commit + real applied patch file names, real vendored nlohmann::json (3.12.0) and cpp-httplib (0.50.1) versions read from their own version macros, real ggml version (0.17.0), and (given --deb) the real Depends: line a specific built package produced (confirmed against an actual built CPU .deb: libc6, libgcc-s1, libgomp1, libstdc++6).
Not a third-party-tool-generated SBOM (no C++/vendored-header equivalent was judged worth adding) -- disclosed as hand-rolled but real-data-sourced, not fabricated.

release_automation_script.label: REAL
evidence: scripts/build-release.sh: configure+build+cpack per requested backend (cpu/vulkan/both), SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH-pinned for reproducibility, one SBOM per built .deb, one SHA256SUMS covering all built .debs. Never touches git in any way (no tag, no push, no `gh release create`).

A real bug was found and fixed while testing this script: the first real run silently produced a near-empty, functionally broken .deb (994 bytes, Installed-Size: 4, no membrane/membrane-run binaries at all) because the script never passed -DMEMBRANE_ENABLE_LLAMA=ON (default OFF) -- fixed, and a permanent sanity check added (`dpkg-deb -c` confirms both real binaries are present before a package is ever copied to the output directory, refusing to publish an empty one again).

A real bash bug was found and fixed: `local a=X b=Y c="...$a..."` referencing an earlier same-statement local variable fails under `set -u` (bash expands all right-hand sides before any assignment takes effect) -- split into separate `local` statements.

Real end-to-end test (CPU backend, this dev host): produced a real .deb containing real membrane/membrane-run binaries, a real SBOM, and a real SHA256SUMS. Two independent runs produced byte-identical .deb output (SHA256 match), confirming the reproducibility fix holds through the full script, not just a bare cpack invocation.
No host OOM during any real build (checked via journalctl); default --jobs 2 chosen deliberately for this memory-constrained dev host, overridable.

signed_tag_policy.label: REAL
evidence: Checked this dev host directly: no git user.signingkey configured, no gpg secret keys present, tag.gpgSign not set.

Policy documented in docs/release-supply-chain.md: never auto-generate a signing key; tag unsigned (real annotated tag) and disclose this plainly in release notes when no real signing identity exists, exactly the state found on this host today.

ci_release_candidate_smoke.label: REAL
evidence: New release-candidate-smoke CI job runs scripts/build-release.sh --backend cpu --out-dir dist on every push/PR, verifies the real .deb/SBOM/SHA256SUMS were produced and sha256sum -c passes, uploads them as a CI artifact. Never calls `gh release create` -- a smoke test of the automation mechanism, not a real release.
Every new/changed CI command (YAML parse, the script itself, the verify block) independently dry-run and confirmed locally before being committed.

known_limitations.label: SOURCE_ANALYSIS
items: scripts/build-release.sh's --backend vulkan/both path is not exercised in CI (2-vCPU/~7GiB GitHub runner cost/time; the existing packaging-smoke job already separately builds a Vulkan .deb without this script) -- it is exercised manually, on a host with the Vulkan SDK, at actual v0.4.0 tagging time (Mega Phase C, PR C4).

The SBOM is hand-rolled (real data, not a third-party-tool output) -- if a genuine C++-ecosystem SBOM standard tool becomes worth adopting later, this script's real, verified data could feed it instead of being superseded speculatively now.
